title: Customer Due Diligence, Officially Valid Documents and Small Accounts

paragraphs.text: Reference is invited to the obligations of banks under the anti-money laundering framework to identify and verify their customers. This circular sets out the Customer Due Diligence (CDD) requirements, the list of Officially Valid Documents (OVDs) and the simplified measures applicable to small accounts, and shall apply to all scheduled commercial banks.

Customer Due Diligence (CDD) for an individual customer shall consist of obtaining the Permanent Account Number or an equivalent declaration, one recent photograph and a certified copy of an Officially Valid Document containing proof of identity and address. Customer Due Diligence shall be completed before any account-based relationship is opened.

Officially Valid Documents (OVDs) for KYC purposes shall mean the passport, the driving licence, the voter identity card and a photo identity card issued by a Central or State Government department to the holder. No other document shall be accepted by a bank as an Officially Valid Document for Customer Due Diligence.

Deemed proof of address: where the Officially Valid Document furnished by a customer does not contain the current address, the bank may accept a utility bill not older than three months or a property tax receipt as deemed proof of address, provided the customer submits an updated OVD within six months.

A small account may be opened for an individual who is unable to furnish an Officially Valid Document, on the basis of a self-attested photograph and a signature or thumb impression affixed in the presence of a bank official. Small accounts shall be opened only at branches connected to the core banking system.

The limits for a small account shall be aggregate credits not exceeding Rs 2,00,000 in a financial year, aggregate withdrawals and transfers not exceeding Rs 20,000 in a month, and a balance not exceeding Rs 75,000 at any time. Foreign inward remittances shall not be credited to a small account.

A small account shall remain operational initially for a period of 18 months and may be continued for a further 12 months only if the account holder furnishes evidence of having applied for an Officially Valid Document. A small account shall be converted to a regular account once full Customer Due Diligence is completed.

The Customer Due Diligence, Officially Valid Document and small account provisions of circular GZ-KYC-2019-01 shall come into force on May 1, 2019 and shall apply to all accounts opened on or after that date.
